description: Stereo reverb in four HP built from eight comb filters and four allpasses, with a chaotic signal generated inside it that can shift the comb delays about

params.text: Sets the size of the space, lengthening the comb delays and the extra taps as it is turned up
Sets how much of the high end is lost on each pass through the reverb, a little at the bottom of its travel and most of it at the top
Sets how long the tail rings on, raising the comb feedback from a half at the bottom of its travel to nearly unity at the top
Crossfades between the signal coming in and the reverb, 0% for the dry signal alone and 100% for the reverb alone
Sets how deeply the chaotic signal shifts the comb delay taps, 0% to 100%; at zero the space holds one fixed shape
Sets how fast the chaotic signal moves, a hundredth of its base speed to twice it

inputs.text: The left side of the signal to be reverberated; with nothing patched to the right jack this one feeds both sides
The right side of the signal to be reverberated
Added to the ROOM knob, a tenth of its travel per volt; the total is held between the two ends of it
Added to the TONE knob, a tenth of its travel per volt; the total is held between the two ends of it
Added to the DECAY knob, a tenth of its travel per volt; the total is held between the two ends of it
Added to the MIX knob, ten points per volt; the total is held between 0% and 100%
Added to the CHAOS knob, ten points per volt; the total is held between 0% and 100%
Added to the RATE knob, a fifth of the base speed per volt; the total is held between a hundredth of it and twice it

outputs.text: The left side of the reverb, crossfaded with the dry signal by MIX
The right side of the reverb, crossfaded with the dry signal by MIX
The chaotic signal itself, ±5V, at the speed set by RATE; the CHAOS knob does not dim it
The chaotic signal sampled and held ten times per unit of the RATE setting, ±5V; the CHAOS knob does not dim it

notes: place this immediately to the right of a YAMANOTE and cables appear on their own: YAMANOTE's send A into the two input jacks, and the two output jacks into its return A.
placing it to the right of another Runner, Facehugger or Ovomorph that is itself beside a YAMANOTE cables it to that YAMANOTE's send and return B instead.
both sides of the reverb are fed from both input jacks, so the two outputs are two views of one space rather than two independent reverbs.
